title: Causal Discovery Methodology Comparison & Strategy Selection

evaluated_approaches.core_principles: Starts with complete undirected graph; deletes edges where X _||_ Y | Z; orients v-structures (colliders) and applies Meek orientation rules.
assumptions: Causal Faithfulness (statistical independence implies absence of direct edge)
Gaussianity or valid non-parametric kernel CI test
strengths: Non-parametric or parametric CI tests support non-linear relationships
PCMCI extension handles autocorrelated time series effectively
weaknesses: High sample-size requirement; fails on short sequences (38-40 steps per run)
High sensitivity to p-value significance threshold alpha (one false CI test error cascades across the entire graph)
Outputs CPDAGs with unoriented undirected edges in Markov equivalence classes
Cannot incorporate physical domain topology masks easily without breaking Meek completeness
evaluated_approaches.treatment_of_temporal_data: Standard PC ignores temporal ordering. PCMCI uses lagged conditional independence tests but requires hundreds of timesteps.
evaluated_approaches.treatment_of_latent_confounding: Standard PC violates guarantees under latent confounding (FCI algorithm required, which produces PAGs with ambiguous circle marks).
evaluated_approaches.computational_complexity: O(N^q) where q is maximum conditioning set size; exponential in worst-case dense graphs.
evaluated_approaches.interpretability: Low-to-moderate; conditional independence p-values provide no quantitative structural equation or effect magnitude.
evaluated_approaches.compatibility_with_interventions: Poor; does not naturally output structural equation parameters required for Pearl's do-operator counterfactual simulation.
evaluated_approaches.suitability_for_causalops: UNSUITABLE for primary engine. 80 experiments x 40 steps is too small for high-power conditional independence tests on 50 variables.

evaluated_approaches.family: Functional causal models via independent component analysis / residual regression
evaluated_approaches.core_principles: Assumes linear structural equation model X = B*X + e where noise terms e_i are non-Gaussian and independent. Exploits non-Gaussianity to uniquely orient all edges and identify B.
assumptions: Linear structural equations: X = B*X + e
strengths: Uniquely identifies the full DAG and structural coefficients (no Markov equivalence ambiguity)
VAR-LiNGAM extends to autoregressive time series X(t) = sum B_k X(t-k) + e(t)
Closed-form structural equations immediately support counterfactual calculations
weaknesses: Strict linearity assumption may miss non-linear saturation thresholds (e.g. pool capacity limits)
Sensitive to noise outliers and near-Gaussian telemetry signals
Does not enforce physical microservice routing constraints unless manually post-thresholded
Unconstrained discovery can produce spurious cross-branch edges under correlated traffic
evaluated_approaches.treatment_of_temporal_data: VAR-LiNGAM explicitly decomposes into contemporaneous (lag 0) and lagged (lag 1..p) structural matrices.
evaluated_approaches.treatment_of_latent_confounding: Latent confounding violates ICA independence, inducing spurious bidirectional edges.
evaluated_approaches.computational_complexity: O(N^4) for iterative regression / mutual information evaluations.
evaluated_approaches.interpretability: High; provides explicit numeric matrix of connection weights B.
evaluated_approaches.compatibility_with_interventions: High; structural matrix B allows direct algebraic evaluation of do(X_i = c) and counterfactual abduction.
evaluated_approaches.suitability_for_causalops: MODERATE-HIGH as a component, but requires hard topological priors to prevent impossible cross-service edges.

evaluated_approaches.family: Score-based structural learning via continuous acyclicity penalty
evaluated_approaches.core_principles: Formulates DAG learning as continuous optimization: min ||X - X*W||_F^2 + lambda*||W||_1 subject to smooth constraint h(W) = Tr(exp(W o W)) - d = 0.
assumptions: Linear or smooth non-linear structural relations
Equal noise variances across nodes (or known scale)
strengths: Replaces combinatorial search over super-exponential DAG space with smooth continuous optimization
DYNOTEARS naturally handles dynamic time series with intra-slice W_0 and inter-slice W_lag matrices
Naturally accommodates prior knowledge via binary mask matrices M (forcing W_ij = 0)
weaknesses: Non-convex optimization; can become trapped in local minima
Under equal noise variance assumption, can falsely invert edge directions if telemetry variances differ widely
Sensitive to hyperparameter tuning (lambda penalty vs rho penalty coefficient)
High compute overhead for large variable counts
evaluated_approaches.treatment_of_temporal_data: DYNOTEARS separates contemporaneous W_0 (subject to h(W_0)=0) and lagged W_lag (unconstrained acyclic by temporal ordering).
evaluated_approaches.treatment_of_latent_confounding: Sensitive; unobserved confounders distort the score landscape.
evaluated_approaches.computational_complexity: O(k * d^3) where k is optimization steps and d is variable count.
evaluated_approaches.interpretability: High; outputs continuous weighted adjacency matrices.
evaluated_approaches.compatibility_with_interventions: High; learned weights W yield structural equation model for simulation.
evaluated_approaches.suitability_for_causalops: VIABLE candidate, but optimization stability and equal-variance assumptions pose reliability risks.

evaluated_approaches.family: Structural Causal Model with Hard Topological Priors & Lagged Autoregressive Dynamics
evaluated_approaches.core_principles: Imposes system-knowledge graph constraints as a hard binary adjacency mask M in {0, 1}^(d x d). Formulates failure propagation as a Time-Lagged Structural Causal Model: X_i(t) = sum_{k=1}^P sum_{j in Parents(i)} A_{ij}^{(k)} X_j(t-k) + B_i X_i(t-1) + epsilon_i(t). Fits structural coefficients via regularized ridge/LASSO regression over topologically allowed pathways.
assumptions: Inter-service propagation strictly follows physical invocation topology and backpressure paths
Temporal Arrow of Time: cause precedes effect by at least tau >= 0 discrete steps
Additive structural equations over operational perturbation ranges
Causal sufficiency within the monitored microservice cluster boundary
strengths: Zero physically implausible edges: impossible shortcuts and cross-branch edges are mathematically forbidden by construction
Acyclicity guaranteed by time-unfolding: unrolling across discrete time steps converts all lagged relations into a strictly acyclic DAG
Optimal sample efficiency: restricts parameter estimation to the sparse set of physically valid connections, eliminating overfitting on 80 experiments
Direct counterfactual engine: Pearl's 3-step abduction-action-prediction reduces to exact matrix algebra
Seamless integration with Phase 2 GNN: provides edge-weight priors and causal validation for neural attention
weaknesses: Requires accurate system call graph topology (readily available in microservice architectures from OpenTelemetry / service mesh)
Does not discover unknown hidden shadow services outside the telemetry boundary
evaluated_approaches.treatment_of_temporal_data: Native discrete-time representation matching the 1.0-second telemetry snapshot cadence of CausalOps.
evaluated_approaches.treatment_of_latent_confounding: Exogenous noise abduction captures unobserved variance without biasing structural topology.
evaluated_approaches.computational_complexity: O(N * d_local * T), highly efficient convex quadratic programming per node.
evaluated_approaches.interpretability: Maximum; every non-zero coefficient corresponds to a verifiable physical service-to-service metric transfer function.
evaluated_approaches.compatibility_with_interventions: Perfect; directly models do(X_s = normal) and computes factual vs counterfactual trajectories.
evaluated_approaches.suitability_for_causalops: OPTIMAL. Selected as the primary causal inference methodology for Phase 3B.

benchmark_comparison_methods: Unconstrained DYNOTEARS (to demonstrate the necessity of topological constraints)
VAR-LiNGAM (to evaluate non-Gaussian orientation without priors)
selection_rationale.justification_summary: In cloud microservice operations, the physical invocation topology is not an unknown black box—it is known engineering fact. Discarding this prior and running unconstrained discovery wastes sample complexity and produces physically nonsensical artifacts (such as database faults directly jumping to payment services). Constraining the lagged SCM with the verified call topology guarantees physical validity, prevents overfitting on the frozen 80-experiment dataset, and provides an exact mathematical engine for counterfactual remediation validation.
